title: Non-text Content
summary: Create a text alternative for visual and auditory content. People who can’t fully see or hear content can understand it.

title: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
summary: Provide an alternative when content is perceivable with only one sense. People who can’t fully see or hear content can understand it.

title: Captions (Prerecorded)
summary: Provide synchronized text for audio content in existing videos. People who are deaf or hard of hearing can understand audio in videos.

title: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
summary: Provide a description of the visual content in videos. People who are blind or who cannot understand the visual content can have it described.

title: Captions (Live)
summary: Provide synchronized text for audio content in real-time videos. People who are deaf or hard of hearing can understand audio in real-time video content.

title: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
summary: Provide a synchronized spoken description of the visual content in videos. People who cannot see or understand the visual content can hear about it while playing videos.

title: Info and Relationships
summary: Use code to reinforce relationships and information conveyed through presentation. People can adapt the presentation to suit their needs while preserving the original meaning.

title: Meaningful Sequence
summary: Use code to preserve meaningful content order. Assistive technology can present content to users in the proper order.

title: Sensory Characteristics
summary: Describe controls by name, not just by appearance or location. People who are blind or have low vision need non-visual instructions.

title: Orientation
summary: Don't lock content to either portrait or landscape presentation. Wheelchair users and others may have devices mounted in a fixed orientation.

title: Identify Input Purpose
summary: Use code to indicate the purpose of common inputs, where technology allows. Some people with cognitive disabilities may not understand the input's purpose from the label alone.

title: Use of Color
summary: Use information in addition to color, such as shape or text, to convey meaning. Not everyone sees colors or sees them the same way.

title: Audio Control
summary: If you play audio content automatically, let people turn it down or off. Sound distracts some people, and also interferes with screen readers.

title: Contrast (Minimum)
summary: Provide sufficient contrast between text and its background. Some people cannot read faint text.

title: Resize Text
summary: Ensure text can be doubled in size. Some people can only read text when it is bigger.

title: Images of Text
summary: Use text instead of pictures of text. People cannot alter how text looks in images.

title: Reflow
summary: Make lines of text reflow within the viewport. People who need bigger text find it difficult if they must scroll to read long lines.

title: Non-text Contrast
summary: Ensure meaningful visual cues achieve 3:1 against the background. Some people cannot see elements with low contrast.

title: Text Spacing
summary: Users can adjust text spacing to make it easier to read. Some people need text with different spacing or font characteristics.

title: Content on Hover or Focus
summary: If hover or focus causes content changes, ensure interaction is predictable. Unpredictable temporary content can be hard for some to consume and may disrupt others.

title: Keyboard
summary: Ensure pointer actions have a keyboard equivalent. Many people rely on the keyboard interface, including blind and some mobility impaired people.

title: No Keyboard Trap
summary: Ensure users always know how to navigate away from components. People who rely on the keyboard often have no other means to navigate.

title: Character Key Shortcuts
summary: Ensure character-only shortcut keys can be turned off or modified. Character-key shortcuts are easy to accidentally trigger, especially with speech input.

title: Timing Adjustable
summary: Let users turn off, adjust, or extend time limits. People with disabilities may need more time to complete activities.

title: Pause, Stop, Hide
summary: Let users control content changes that occur in parallel with other content. Some people with cognitive disabilities and attention deficits are distracted by continuous movement.

title: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
summary: Avoid content that flashes, or keep it under thresholds. Flashing content can cause migraines, dizziness, nausea, and seizures.

title: Bypass Blocks
summary: Provide a means of skipping repeating content. Users reliant on the keyboard interface can move around pages efficiently.

title: Page Titled
summary: Provide a descriptive page title using appropriate technology. Page titles help users identify and distinguish different pages.

title: Focus Order
summary: Elements receive focus in an order that preserves meaning. Navigating a site or application with only the keyboard will make sense.

title: Link Purpose (In Context)
summary: Provide descriptive names or context for all links. People with visual and cognitive disabilities can navigate more easily.

title: Multiple Ways
summary: Provide at least two options for reaching the same content. Not everyone can navigate content in the same way.

title: Headings and Labels
summary: Provide descriptive headings and labels People can orient themselves, especially those with cognitive or visual disabilities.

title: Focus Visible
summary: Ensure each item receiving focus has a visible indicator. Without a focus indicator, sighted keyboard users cannot operate the page.

title: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
summary: Ensure when an item gets keyboard focus, it is at least partially visible. People who can't use a mouse need to see what has keyboard focus.

title: Pointer Gestures
summary: Provide single-point operation for all functions. Not everyone can perform complex and multi-touch gestures.

title: Pointer Cancellation
summary: Make pointer cancellation predictable and consistent. Make it easier for anyone to recover from something they didn’t mean to do.

title: Label in Name
summary: Where practical, make the control’s text label and name match. People who operate with voice interaction use the visible labels in their commands.

title: Motion Actuation
summary: Don't rely solely on device motion to control page content. Some people cannot hold or move a device steadily.

title: Dragging Movements
summary: For any action that involves dragging, provide a simple pointer alternative. Some people cannot use a mouse to drag items.

title: Target Size (Minimum)
summary: Ensure targets meet a minimum size or have sufficient spacing around them. Some people with physical impairments cannot click small buttons that are close together.

title: Language of Page
summary: Indicate the predominant language on a page. People using assistive technology get information in the correct language.

title: Language of Parts
summary: Indicate when words are in a different language. People using assistive technology get information in the correct language.

title: On Focus
summary: Do not change a user's context when items get focus. Content that behaves predictably is especially important to people with disabilities.

title: On Input
summary: Forewarn users if their context will change based on their input. Content that behaves predictably is especially important to people with disabilities.

title: Consistent Navigation
summary: Consistently order navigation that repeats across multiple pages. Content that behaves predictably is especially important to people with disabilities.

title: Consistent Identification
summary: Consistently identify components that have the same functionality throughout a set of web pages. Consistent identification helps users recognize familiar functionality when it appears on different web pages, making websites easier to learn, navigate, and use.

title: Consistent Help
summary: Put help in the same place when it is on multiple pages. People who need help can find it more easily if it's in the same place.

title: Error Identification
summary: Provide descriptive notification of errors. Flagging errors helps people with reduced sight and cognitive disabilities resolve them.

title: Labels or Instructions
summary: Provide labels or instructions for inputs. Everyone, especially those with cognitive disabilities, will know how to respond.

title: Error Suggestion
summary: Where errors are detected, suggest known ways to correct them. People can address errors faster and with reduced effort.

title: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
summary: Provide ways for users to confirm, correct, or reverse important submissions. People with disabilities may be more likely to make mistakes, or not notice them.

title: Redundant Entry
summary: Don't ask for the same information twice in the same activity. Some people with cognitive disabilities have difficulty remembering what they entered before.

title: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
summary: Don't make people solve, recall, or transcribe something to log in. Some people with cognitive disabilities cannot solve puzzles, memorize a username and password, or retype one-time passcodes.

title: Name, Role, Value
summary: Give components correct names, roles, states, and values. Assistive technology only works well when code is done properly.

title: Status Messages
summary: Let assistive technology notify users about status changes that don't take focus. People who do not see messages need to be informed about them.
